title: Field factors and integral generators of a quadratic coefficient series algebra
statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $\beta,\gamma\in F$ with $\beta^2-4\gamma\ne0$. Put $p(Z)=Z^2+\beta Z+\gamma$, $L=F[Z]/(p)$, let $z$ be the class of $Z$, and set $B=L[[t]]$ and $A=F+tB$, with $F$ embedded as constant series. Polynomial rings, power series, and quotients use [def-weil-polynomial-ring], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].
If $p$ has a root $r\in F$, then $s=-\beta-r$ is a distinct second root and evaluation at $r,s$ induces an $F$-algebra isomorphism $L\cong F\times F$. If $p$ has no root in $F$, then $L$ is a field of degree two over $F$. Thus there are $m\in\{1,2\}$ and field extensions $K_i/F$ with an $F$-algebra isomorphism $L\cong\prod_{i=1}^mK_i$, whose coefficientwise extension is an isomorphism
$$B\cong\prod_{i=1}^mD_i,\qquad D_i=K_i[[t]],$$
sending $t$ to the tuple of power-series variables. Every $D_i$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field $E_i=\operatorname{Frac}(D_i)$, meaning that every fraction satisfying a monic polynomial over $D_i$ lies in $D_i$. Hence $B$ is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent elements).
Every $h\in B$ has a unique expression $h=u+zv$ with $u,v\in F[[t]]\subseteq A$, and satisfies
$$h^2+(\beta v-2u)h+(u^2-\beta uv+\gamma v^2)=0.$$
In particular $1,z$ generate $B$ as an $A$-module, so $B$ is finite over $A$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and every element of $B$ is integral over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Multiplication by $t$ is injective on $B$ and on $A$. These assertions include characteristic two and the split case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] to the monic degree-two polynomial $p$. Thus $1,z$ are an $F$-basis of $L$: each element is uniquely $a+bz$ with $a,b\in F$. In particular the scalar map $F\to L$ is injective and $\dim_F L=2$. The quotient relation is $z^2=-\beta z-\gamma$.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof of (1) implies (2), Cases I and II; explicit coefficient-algebra calculations expanding the two displayed normalization models.

proof.text: If $p(r)=0$, set $s=-\beta-r$. Then $rs=\gamma$, $p=(Z-r)(Z-s)$, and $(r-s)^2=\beta^2-4\gamma\ne0$, so $r\ne s$. Evaluation descends to an $F$-algebra map $L\to F\times F$. On the basis coordinates it is $a+bz\mapsto(a+br,a+bs)$, with inverse $(c,d)\mapsto (rd-sc)/(r-s)+((c-d)/(r-s))z$. Substitution gives both inverse identities. This proves the split assertion without invoking a further Chinese-remainder result.

If $p$ has no root, let $w=a+bz

Take $m=1$, $K_1=L$ in this case, and $m=2$, $K_1=K_2=F$ in step 2. No division by $2$ has been used.

proof.text: Write $\phi:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i K_i$ for the resulting algebra isomorphism. Define $\Phi:B\to\prod_iK_i[[t]]$ by $\Phi(\sum_n h_nt^n)_i=\sum_n\phi(h_n)_it^n$. Its inverse sends $(\sum_n a_{i,n}t^n)_i$ to $\sum_n\phi^{-1}((a_{i,n})_i)t^n$. These maps are inverse coefficientwise. They preserve addition and multiplication because each coefficient of a product is the finite sum $\sum_{j=0}^n h_jh_{n-j}$. Constants are preserved and $t$ maps to $(t)_i.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof of (1) implies (2), Cases I and II; explicit coefficient-algebra calculations expanding the two displayed normalization models.

proof.text: Each field $K_i$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $K_i$, generated by $0$ and $1$. It is a normal domain, since every fraction $a/b$ with $b\ne0$ already equals $ab^{-1}\in K_i$. These verify the hypotheses, using [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-normal-domain]. That node gives that $D_i=K_i[[t]]$ is an integral domain and is integrally closed in $E_i=\operatorname{Frac}(D_i)$. If $h\in B$ has $h^n=0$ for $n\ge1$, each component of $\Phi(h)$ has zero $n$-th power and hence is zero in its domain; injectivity of $\Phi$ gives $h=0$. Thus $B$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), statement, applied to a field; the nilpotent calculation in a product of domains is elementary.

proof.text: For $h=\sum_n h_nt^n$, write the unique coordinates from step 1 as $h_n=a_n+zb_n$ and set $u=\sum_n a_nt^n$, $v=\sum_n b_nt^n$ in $F[[t]]$. Then $h=u+zv$, uniquely by comparing coefficients. The scalar series map $F[[t]]\to B$ is injective coefficientwise. Every scalar series $u$ equals $a_0+t\sum_n a_{n+1}t^n$, so belongs to $A=F+tB$. This is a subring, since $tB$ is an ideal of $B$ and scalar constants form a subring.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof of (1) implies (2), Cases I and II; explicit coefficient-algebra calculations expanding the two displayed normalization models.

proof.text: Using $z^2=-\beta z-\gamma$, expand $(u+zv)(u-\beta v-zv)=u^2-\beta uv+\gamma v^2$. The second factor equals $2u-\beta v-h$, so rearrangement gives the displayed monic equation $h^2+(\beta v-2u)h+(u^2-\beta uv+\gamma v^2)=0$. Its coefficients lie in $F[[t]]\subseteq A$. Hence every $h$ is integral over $A$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Also $h=u\cdot1+v\cdot z$ has coefficients in $A$, so $1,z$ generate $B$ as an $A$-module and it is finite by [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof of (1) implies (2), Cases I and II; explicit coefficient-algebra calculations expanding the two displayed normalization models.

proof.text: Finally multiplication by $t$ shifts coefficients: for $h=\sum_n h_nt^n$, the constant coefficient of $th$ is zero and its coefficient in degree $n+1$ is $h_n$. Thus $th=0$ forces $h=0$, and multiplication by $t$ is injective on $B$. Since $t\in tB\subseteq A$ and $A\subseteq B$, its restriction is injective on $A$. All coefficient and norm identities above are ring identities valid also in characteristic two and in the product case.
